title: Get It in Writing
description:
Don't rely on "probably." See what an official page actually promises — and get the gap confirmed in writing.





Websites are full of sentences that sound like promises — "free cancellation," "connecting rooms available upon request." People book, buy, and rent believing them. Get It in Writing checks what a business actually promises before you spend your money, and gets the rest confirmed in writing.

**How it works**

1. Paste the official page you're about to rely on and state what must be true.
2. Firecrawl reads only the provider's own site; OpenAI classifies every requirement against captured source passages — established, conditional, conflicting, scope mismatch, or not established — every claim backed by a verbatim excerpt.
3. If a consequential gap remains, the app drafts one precise email to a source-verified official contact. Nothing sends without the owner approving the exact recipient and wording (AgentMail).
4. The real written reply is interpreted requirement by requirement into a private Proof Card that preserves the answer, its exact conditions, and the original message. Sources stay monitored afterward — if the official page changes, both versions stay visible until acknowledged.

**Convex under the hood**: realtime queries drive every screen; the case state machine runs on mutations, scheduled functions, and crons; HTTP actions receive AgentMail webhooks; components: @agentmail/convex, @firecrawl/firecrawl-convex, @convex-dev/rate-limiter, @convex-dev/static-hosting; Convex Auth with a shared judge wallet.

**Nothing simulated**: the demo wallet's cases are real pipeline runs — including a written reply from a real hotel conversation and a Proof Card confirmed in writing by the product's own maker. The 90-second video films the live product, research run included.

**For judges**: sign in with the shared demo wallet — email [judge@getitinwriting.demo](mailto:judge@getitinwriting.demo), password dont-rely-on-probably. You can create a decision and watch the research pipeline live (the form offers a one-click worked example); sending, editing, and deleting stay with the owner. Public sign-ups are closed behind a waitlist during judging so shared budgets stay protected.

**Challenges we ran into**: HTML-only email replies arrived with empty text and were mis-scored as unresponsive — inbound processing now converts HTML to text and hydrates the stored thread over the AgentMail API before interpretation. And keeping the pipeline honest: the classifier refused three seeded phrasings until the wording matched the page's actual published words — that refusal is the product working.

title: Attest
description:
An assistant on your inbox that says yes to the verified recruiter and the small invoice, and no to the SSN scam and the unverified wire.



## The problem

We're starting to let AI agents run our inboxes for applying to jobs, replying to recruiters, handling the back-and-forth. But your agent can't tell a real recruiter from a scam any better than you can, and a job search is exactly where you're asked for sensitive info (salary, availability, references, even your SSN for a "background check") over and over.

## How it works

For every email, Attest asks one question: **did this actually come from who it claims?** It grades every sender from real email authentication (DMARC), then decides both ways:

- **YES** for a _verified_ recruiter asks for your availability and salary range? You approved sharing those once, so it answers for you. A _verified_ $20 invoice under your limit? It pays it.
- **NO** for an SSN request? Held, always, even from a verified sender (sensitive info can never be auto-shared). A $5,000 wire from an address that never authenticated? Held.

The difference is provable: the **same** info request from an _unverified_ sender holds. Verification is what unlocks the yes.

## Notable features

- Deterministic policy gate with **no LLM in the decision path** so that it can't be talked into a mistake by clever wording
- A live trust **registry** (A–F grades earned from authenticated mail, not SEO), exposed as a public API
- A 3D **trust graph**: verified hubs (Greenhouse, Lever) vouch for the companies that reach you through them
- One-click **"Load demo data"** that seeds a live inbox through the real pipeline + a guided tour

## Why I built it

Anyone can be fooled by a convincing fake, and the people most at risk (older or less technical family members) most of all. An agent that holds your details should refuse to hand them over unless it can prove who's asking.

## Tech stack

Convex (backend, live queries, auth, HTTP API, scheduled functions, hosting), AgentMail (real agent inbox), Firecrawl (enrich each sender), OpenAI (typed extraction), React + Vite, TypeScript.

## Challenges

Making the gate provably safe: sensitive info (SSN/bank) can never auto-release even from a verified sender with a containment guarantee we back with tests. 156 unit + integration tests, including ground-truth gates and cross-tenant isolation. It's also the working implementation of three published research papers on agent trust.

title: Recourse
description:
Pursue what you're owed, citing the clause that entitles you to it.





## The problem

Most people are owed something they never chase. A duplicate charge, a deposit
kept back, an appliance that died inside warranty. Chasing it means finding the
right policy, writing a letter that cannot be dismissed, and following up for
weeks. So the money stays unclaimed.

A claim that says "this is unfair" gets a form response. A claim that quotes
clause 9.2 of the company's own returns policy back at them, by number, gets
routed to someone who can settle it. The hard part is that the governing
provision is one paragraph buried in a forty page document nobody has read.

## How it works

1. **It reads their terms.** Firecrawl maps the counterparty's domain and every
URL is scored against the paths a claim is actually argued from. Product
pages, browse trees and anything carrying a SKU are rejected, so it reads the
four pages that matter instead of buying a whole website.
2. **And the law above them.** It looks up the statutory rights that override
whatever the company wrote, accepting results only from official sources.
A law firm's summary of a statute is not the statute.
3. **It finds the clauses.** Each document is mined for individually citable
provisions, kept verbatim with the document's own reference, and marked as
supporting or opposing the claim. It keeps the exclusions too, because the
provision they will quote back is worth knowing before the letter goes out.
4. **It writes the letter.** Cited by reference, stating one amount and one
deadline, pre-empting the strongest opposing provision. Every citation is
bound to the clause record it came from, so hovering one in the interface
lights up its source.
5. **It corresponds.** Sent from its own inbox via AgentMail. Replies arrive by
signed webhook and are read for what was committed to rather than how warmly
it was said: an apology carrying no decision is an acknowledgement, not a
concession.
6. **It chases.** An hourly sweep advances stalled claims along a four rung
escalation ladder. Each rung is a different letter, not the same letter sent
louder.

Nothing leaves the outbox without a human approving it.

## Notable features

- **Traceable citations.** Hover a reference in the letter and its source clause
highlights. Every judge has seen an LLM invent a citation; this is the answer.
- **It argues both sides.** It extracts the provisions that work against the
claim and disarms them in advance: _"Although \[5.\] says payment is taken when_
_an order is submitted, that does not authorise a second charge for the same_
_order."_
- **Real two-way email.** Replies land on the case live. Evidence can be
attached and goes out on the same thread when they ask for a receipt.
- **Failures are visible.** A bounce or a spam complaint closes the case and
stops the chase, because a claim sent to a dead address that sits looking
healthy is the worst failure for a tool that promised to chase for you.

## Why I built it

Because the paperwork is the barrier, not the entitlement. The rights already
exist. What is missing is anyone with the time to read the policy and write the
letter.

## Tech stack

- **Convex** for database, functions, real-time sync, crons, scheduler, HTTP
actions, file storage, full-text and vector search. Seven tables, fifteen
indexes, eight components including two workpools tuned differently: one wide
for crawl fan-out, one deliberately narrow for outbound mail.
- **Firecrawl** for domain mapping, policy scraping and statutory lookup.
- **AgentMail** for inbox identity, signed webhook ingest and threaded replies.
- **OpenAI** for clause extraction, letter drafting, reply comprehension and
embeddings.
- React 19, Vite, Tailwind v4, Motion and GSAP, served by Convex static hosting.

## Challenges

**The AgentMail component is half-broken on Convex 1.45.** Everything it exposes
as an

```
internalAction
```

fails to resolve from the parent app, including

```
performSend
```

, so queued mail could never be delivered. Its queries and
mutations resolve fine. Outbound now goes through a small REST client against
the same endpoints, while the component keeps signed webhook ingest and the
reactive message store.

**Silent failures cost the most time.** Every colour class was written in
Tailwind v3 arbitrary syntax, which v4 compiles to nothing without warning: 126
references rendering as unstyled defaults while the custom properties were all
present in the output. A URL scorer matching substrings read "noisecancelling"
as a cancellation policy and paid to scrape a headphones listing. Citation
references failed to match across

```
[5.]
```

and

```
5.
```

, so letters looked sourced
while being untraceable. All three are now regression tests.

**Deploying the wrong bundle.**

```
upload --prod
```

without

```
--build
```

publishes the
local dist, and that dist was built against the dev backend. The production URL
was reading and writing dev data for hours.

## Metrics

Verified end to end on production, not mocked: 497 URLs mapped, 4 documents
selected with no product noise, 35 citable provisions extracted across a
retailer's terms and the Consumer Rights Act 2015, a letter binding 3 citations
to their sources, a real email delivered, and a human reply routed back and
classified in 6 seconds. 40 commits, 36 tests passing.

title: TableForAll
description:
Email replies become a cited dinner shortlist. Guests install nothing.





### Problem you're solving

Group dinners fail in the group chat. The organizer is constantly repeating questions, trying to compare restaurants, cross-referencing allergies, and chasing people down for their votes. It quickly becomes overwhelming, and making a decision that accommodates everyone's budget, location, and dietary needs is a logistical nightmare. TableForAll solves this by turning unstructured email replies into one live, actionable decision.

### How the app works

A host starts a single dinner plan. Instead of forcing guests to download yet another app or join a new group chat, guests simply reply to an email. As replies come in, OpenAI extracts structured constraints from their natural language responses—dates, budgets, locations, and dietary needs. Firecrawl uses these constraints to automatically research and evaluate venue sites. Meanwhile, Convex aggregates this data and keeps a live, real-time shortlist and vote tally updated for everyone. AgentMail handles verified inbox access to securely poll for those guest replies.

### Notable features

- **Zero-Friction Guest Experience:** Guests reply natively via email without needing to install an app or create an account.
- **AI Constraint Extraction:** OpenAI structured outputs accurately parse messy, natural-language emails into strict dietary, budget, and availability constraints.
- **Automated Venue Research:** Firecrawl v2 actively scrapes restaurant websites, menus, and hours to evaluate venue fit and provide cited sources.
- **Real-Time Polling & Shortlists:** Powered by Convex, the app state (votes, constraints, research) updates instantly across all connected clients.
- **Privacy-First Demo Mode:** Built with a marked interactive preview that runs end-to-end tests without sending unsolicited emails to outside recipients.

### Why did you build this

We wanted to build an "everyday app"—something that solves a universal, frustrating problem that real people deal with every week. We chose this after comparing several ideas because it perfectly highlights the power of our sponsor stack: using AI to bring structure to the chaos of group coordination, while keeping the user interface completely invisible to the guests (via email).

### Tech stack list

```
Backend & Real-time Sync: Convex
AI & Extraction: OpenAI (Structured Outputs)
Data Scraping & Research: Firecrawl v2
Email Infrastructure: AgentMail
Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite
```

### Challenges we ran into

One of our biggest challenges was **safety and accuracy**—specifically, making sure the AI didn't hallucinate an allergy guarantee that could put a guest at risk. Restaurant sites can be incomplete or stale. We overcame this by strictly enforcing cited sources via Firecrawl and designing the UI to always display the source link, explicitly reminding hosts to confirm severe allergies directly with the venue rather than trusting the extraction blindly. We also had to aggressively scope our MVP boundary (sticking to dinner only, one city, three venues, and one vote) to ensure we shipped a complete, working loop in time.

### Any success stories or metrics

- **Successful End-to-End Live Calls:** Fully integrated and passed live calls across Convex, OpenAI, Firecrawl, and AgentMail by August 28th.
- **Demo Safety:** We successfully implemented a public demo path that verifies AgentMail scoped access and runs OpenAI structured extraction on a marked "safety reply" without sending a single real email, making it safe for judges to test aggressively.
- **100% Type Safe:** Passed all strict linting, type checks, and tests across the full-stack Convex and React environment prior to deployment!
